terms.meaning: A self-similar shape: small parts look like the whole. They are found in nature and in art.
A flat shape that folds up to make a solid.
A view of a solid on a flat surface, like its shadow. The usual ones are the front, top and side views.
A view of a cube turned so that all its edges look equal in length. It can be drawn on isometric grid paper.
A face is a flat side, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner.

items.name: Sierpinski carpet
items.example: Each square becomes 9 and the middle is removed. Step 2: 8² = 64 squares.

items.name: Sierpinski gasket
items.example: Each triangle becomes 4 and the middle is removed. Step 3: 3³ = 27 triangles.

items.name: Koch snowflake
items.example: Step 2: 3 × 4² = 48 sides, each 1/9 as long as a starting side.

items.name: Prism with an n-sided base
items.example: Triangular prism, n = 3: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices.

items.name: Pyramid with an n-sided base
items.example: Square pyramid, n = 4: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices.

items.name: Nets of a cube
items.example: Nets that are only turned or flipped copies of each other count as one.

items.name: Net of a cylinder
items.example: The rectangle's length equals the circle's circumference.

items.name: Shortest path on a cuboid
items.formula: Unfold it into a net and draw a straight line
items.example: On a net, a path with sides 24 cm and 32 cm has length √(24² + 32²) = 40 cm.

items.name: Three standard views
items.formula: Front view, top view and side view
items.example: A cylinder standing up: the top view is a circle, and the front view is a rectangle.

mistakes.text: A solid can have more than one net. A cube has 11, so check by folding it in your mind.
The net you choose changes the path. Try all the unfoldings and pick the shortest.
Do not mix up a prism and a pyramid. A prism has two bases and 3n edges; a pyramid has one base and 2n edges.
Different objects can have the same projection, so one view is not enough to know the solid.
